name: Blade Temperature
body:
The gold blade is going to get a little hotter as it is bigger and has a larger surface area. Be sure to oil it to keep it running cooler but the heat is similar to other comparable clippers.

If you are looking for the coolest operation you want to use the shallow tooth blade which has a smaller contact of surface area and will therefore not get as warm.

For the absolute coolest operation you could try our double black diamond shallow tooth combo which will have the coolest operation of any.

name: Switch fix - 2 versions
body:
Please follow the steps below.

1. Take off the Clipper lid (3 screws on the front of clipper)
2. You will then see 2 screws on the face of the switch. Please take the two screws off, take off the switch lid, and take out the switch lever piece with the metal conductor attached. It should look like the image below. 



3.Using a cloth or a brush thoroughly wipe the pieces of the switch so no hairs interfere with the connection. If you see any product residue, please use alcohol/disinfectant to clean the surface.

Please ensure that the two switch screws are tightened before assembling it back into your clippers. 

If this did not solve your issue we'd be happy to send you a replacement switch, please let me know your shipping information. 

OR

I am sorry to hear you are having this issue. However, We have a very simple and easy fix to this problem. Please follow the steps below.

1. Take off the Clipper lid (3 screws on the front of clipper)
2. You will then see 2 screws on the face of the switch Please ensure they are both tightened fully using a small phillips head screwdriver. 
3.Using a cloth or a brush thoroughly wipe the face of the switch so no hairs interfere with the connection. 

Please be sure to fully disassemble the switch to clean it if tightening the screws does not solve the issue as there may be hair build up in the switch. 

Due to the vibration of the clipper these screws tend to come loose from time to time. Hair also tends to build up in the switch, causing the switch to malfunction. These steps solve the problem most of the time.

If this does not resolve the issue, we would be happy to send you a replacement switch. Please provide a good shipping address.

name: Trimmer Blades Smoking
body:
It is not uncommon for a new trimmer to smoke when it is first taken out of the box.
This is because many trimmers require an oiling and break-in period before they can function properly. While it may be concerning to see smoke coming from your new trimmer, it is
generally nothing to worry about. In fact, it is a sign that your trimmer is getting the necessary lubrication and is breaking in properly. As long as the smoking stops after a few minutes of use, there is no need for concern. However, if the smoking persists, it is best to contact our customer service team for further assistance.

name: Uno Cutter Difference & Not Cutting Very Well
body:
Uno shaver comes with two cutters; one forged cutter (black ), and one crunchy cutter (red). The forged cutter is a standard cutting blade, and the crunchy cutter creates a crunchy noise when you use the shaver. We recommend switching them out according to your preference! 

We recommend replacing the blades and the foil approximately every three months (if it is used frequently). Please note that it is very important to replace the cutters/foils, since when they start to become dull, it can cause painful razor burns, or the foils can break and damage the skin. We recommend using the shaver on short stubble hair, and it will not work as well on long, or thin hair. It is the best for balding head scalp, or for mens coarse facial hair. For the smoothest shave, we recommend using a trimmer, and going over the area with the  Uno shaver. I hope this helps!

name: Blade Smoking
body:
Some of you might notice a strange "smoke" coming from your trimmers. Don't worry! This is a result of the dry blade, not the trimmer body. You'll also be glad to know that your blade won't get hot at all.
If you encounter this, there's an easy fix: ensure the blade is clean, then apply 2-3 drops of the included clipper oil. The smoke will disappear within seconds. We've tested this extensively, and it's simply a byproduct of the dry blade and its coating.
If you have any further questions about maintenance, please don't hesitate to contact us.

name: Difference Between Regular & Tight Guards
body: Tight guards have skinnier, thinner teeth. It makes it easier to blend and you will have less lines in the hair. End result “blurrier fades”.

name: Ridges On Blades
body:
The ridges on a fixed hair clipper blade help guide hair into the moving blades, but they do it in different ways. Blades with higher ridges have more metal, which naturally helps disperse heat, keeping them cooler during use. This design also improves airflow and reduces friction, making for a smoother, more efficient cut.  

More information about the shallow and high ridges:

High ridges are better for barbers cutting dense, thick, or curly hair.
Shallow ridges work well for fine hair, precision fades, or sensitive scalps.

name: Blade Cutting Length
body:
With the tight bracket on, the clipper will open to a 0.5 with any blade.
Additionally, with the stretch bracket on, the clipper will open to a full 1 with any blade.
When zero gapped with our blade setting tool, the clipper can be adjusted to 0.3mm.
Our clipper guards will be compatible with any clipper blades.

While it's optimized for three devices, you can connect more — such as up to 5 devices — without causing any damage or performance issues. The only trade-off is longer charging times, typically over 6 hours when more than three devices are connected.

name: Zero Gapping Info
body: The moving blade should never pass the fixed blade when zero gapping. It should be straight and leveled just enough where you see a spec of the fixed blade protecting both consumer and guards. Lever should also be set on the lowest level when zero gapping.

name: Question about Vector Motor
body:
The linear vector motor provides consistent, intuitive torque, with speed controlled by an integrated chip (IC). At idle, the motor runs at approximately 8000 RPM (±500 RPM), and under load, it can reach up to 11,000 RPM. The most noticeable speed increase happens while cutting hair—this is completely normal and part of the motor's design.
Variations in speed between hair trimmers are also completely normal. These can result from differences in blade combinations, clipper maintenance, or even usage conditions. To maintain optimal performance, ensure the blades are clean and properly oiled.

name: Rebel Shaver Foils
body:
The Rebel is equipped with precision "crunch" cutting blades, which are designed for a close and powerful shave. However, these blades generate more friction than traditional ones, making regular maintenance especially important. To help prevent premature wear and protect the foil from developing holes, it’s essential to apply a drop or two of blade oil before or after each use. This keeps the blades gliding smoothly, minimizes heat buildup, and significantly extends the life of both the blades and foil.
If the foil is already showing signs of damage, it could be due to prolonged dry operation or debris buildup, which increases friction and weakens the mesh. We recommend replacing the foil if any holes are present, as continued use may lead to skin irritation or further damage.
Please let us know if you need help sourcing a replacement foil or if you’d like guidance on how to properly maintain your shaver going forward. We're here to help.

name: Blade Gets Hot
body:
Thank you for reaching out. Please follow the steps below: 
Oil the blade: Apply 1–2 drops of clipper oil to the blade while the unit is running, then wipe away any excess.
Check blade alignment: Ensure the moving cutter is aligned evenly with the fixed blade and is not extending past it.
Clean the blade: Remove the blade and brush away any hair or debris, including underneath the cutter.
Check blade tension: If the blade screws are too tight, the cutter may not move freely. Slightly loosen the screws and test again.
Inspect for blade damage: Look for chipped, bent, or dull blade teeth, which may require replacement.
Some warmth is normal, but if the blades get very hot, burn the skin, or overheat quickly, this may indicate a service issue. Please let us know if this continues so we can assist further.

name: Difference Between Clippers & Trimmers
body: The difference between clippers and trimmers, clippers are generally bigger, and have rectangular blades. They are more powerful than trimmers, and can handle bulk hair or length removals, and covers larger surface area, so it is great for fades. Trimmers are smaller, and they are great for trimming the neck or beard areas. Since it is smaller, it can also be used towards the end of your hair cut to line up the edges of your hairline, or any other finishing touch ups. If you have any other questions please let me know!

In some cases hair clippers can be completely clogged with hair, causing the temperature to rise rapidly; furthermore, the blades may lack lubrication.

name: Product Recommendation / Which Model Should I Buy
body:
Thank you for your interest in our products! The right tool depends on how you plan to use it: clippers are designed for bulk cutting and fading with guards, while trimmers are made for lining, edging, and detail work.

For an all-around professional clipper we recommend the Instinct or the Ergo series, and for crisp line work the Saber trimmer is our most popular choice. You can compare all models and their features here:
https://stylecraftus.com/collections/all

If you tell us a little more about how you plan to use the tool (home use or professional, fading, lining, or full cuts), we would be happy to give you a specific recommendation. Have a great day!

name: Clipper Maintenance & Oiling
body:
Thank you for reaching out. Regular maintenance will keep your clipper running like new. We recommend the following routine:

1. Brush hair and debris off the blade after every use.
2. Apply 2-3 drops of clipper oil across the blade teeth and one drop on each side rail, then run the clipper for a few seconds so the oil spreads evenly. Do this daily with regular use.
3. Wipe away excess oil with a clean cloth.
4. Avoid submerging the clipper or blade in water or spray disinfectant directly into the motor housing.

Keeping the blade oiled prevents heat, pulling, and premature wear. If your blade is still underperforming after a proper cleaning and oiling, let us know and we will be happy to troubleshoot further. Have a great day!
